speaker: Doctor
text:
I need to clarify the timeline of your symptoms: did the walking difficulties, incontinence, and speech issues start all at once, or did one appear before the others? Also, have you noticed any issues with your sense of taste or smell?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Creatine_Kinase.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Appearance Clear, WBC 0-5 /HPF, RBC 0-2 /HPF, Nitrites Negative, Leukocyte_Esterase Negative; Creatine_Kinase: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive difficulty walking. I also have Urinary incontinence, Slurred speech, Rigidity in limbs, Mild hand tremor, Orthostatic hypotension.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Unremarkable. No known chronic diseases. Social history: Occasionally consumes alcohol. Non-smoker. Works as a bank clerk.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent infections, fever, weight loss, vision changes or seizures. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Cellulitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is confusing, as cellulitis typically presents with localized skin infection and redness, not progressive walking difficulties, incontinence, or speech issues. Did you experience numbness or tingling in your legs before the walking problems began?

REQUEST TEST: MRI_Spine, MRI_Brain.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Brain_and_Spinal_Cord: Multiple areas of atrophy and signal changes in the brainstem, cerebellum, and basal ganglia, consistent with neurodegenerative processes.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple Sclerosis (MS). While the MRI findings are consistent with neurodegenerative processes, the specific combination of brainstem, cerebellum, and basal ganglia involvement alongside your progressive symptoms suggests a demyelinating disease like MS. I recommend an MRI of the orbits to check for optic neuritis, which is a common associated finding.
